newsitem.title: ITALY: Autostrade sale must be transparent-head.
newsitem.headline: Autostrade sale must be transparent-head.

text.p: The privatisation of Italian motorway operator Autostrade must be completely transparent and carried out in such a way that the group does not fall into "untrustworthy hands", its chairman said.

Giancarlo Elia Valori said terms and conditions of the market placement should be set very carefully "to prevent the company suddenly ending up in untrustworthy hands, given the alarming dimensions of money laundering taking place on stock markets."
He was speaking at a meeting in northern Italy of Autostrade franchise holders, a statement from the group said.

Italy's state industrial holding IRI wants to sell off Autostrade by the end of this year but a regulatory authority for the transport sector, a necessary pre-privatisation step, has yet to be created.

Apart from the watchdog authority, Valori said that to protect public interests in the national motorway sector "criteria of absolute objectivity and clarity are essential in order to fix a value for the company."
"I will only be reassured when there are sufficient guarantees that the sale can go through in the most complete transparency," he added.
